metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5) over 5+ days, model under-responds; add 1–3% bias to forecast to counteract mean reversion.
- Model frequently under-estimates true outcomes in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead); apply 1–4% upward bias for first 5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% starting from day 7–10.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by > 10% in 30d, check if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior — if yes, apply 2–5% downward bias for next 30d to avoid overcorrection.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings > 0.5 in 3 consecutive days, add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast range.
